key_insight: OpenGEM26 expands molecular force-field training with 4.4 million DFT-labeled conformations, enabling GPTFF-mol to learn more accurate organic-molecule energies and forces across broad non-equilibrium geometries.
engineering_relevance: The resulting graph neural network potential offers a faster surrogate for DFT molecular simulation, especially for sulfur- and chlorine-containing organics in conformational and reaction-barrier studies.
method: Generated OpenGEM26: 200,000 unique molecules and 4.4 million conformations with H/C/N/O/S/Cl atoms.
Computed structures along complete optimization trajectories using ωB97X-D with Def2-SVP/Def2-TZVP and dispersion corrections.
Trained the GPTFF-mol graph neural network potential and benchmarked it on torsions, tautomerization, and force prediction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an energy MAE of 16 meV/molecule (0.82 meV/atom), superior force performance to ANI-2x, and improved coverage of energy, bond-length, and bond-angle space versus QM9.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on molecules with up to ten heavy atoms, so transferability to larger or chemically more diverse systems may require additional validation.
paper_title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields (GPTFF-mol) for Organic Molecules from Optimization Trajectories (OpenGEM26)
